title: Illumination flares: fight by flarelight at night
summary: At night men see only a short way. Mortars now fire star shells: magnesium flares that drift down under parachutes, light the ground and everyone on it, and throw shadows that swing as they fall. The AI lights up night attacks too.
stage: Native Godot 4.7.2 Forward+, --scenario=flares --static --seed=1 (night), High preset, --fixed-fps 30, 1280x720, command camera --focus=0,-8 --zoom=45 --pitch=-12 --nohud. FL_DEBUG_FLARE_AT=-44,-45,3 bursts one flare over (-44, -45) at t=3 so it drifts low past the wall in its last seconds; clip = 300 frames from t=32 (--shot-at=32 --shots=300 --shot-every=0.03333). Without-flare frame: same run with FL_DEBUG_FLARES_HIDE=1 at t=37. Swing stills: clip frames 90 (t=35, swing -1.0 m) and 150 (t=37, +0.8 m), cropped.
rationale: A flare is light that moves: the clip shows the drift, the swing and the shadows swinging with it; the matched with/without pair shows the pool and its falloff; the swing pair shows the shadows moving. Measured on a wide matched pair (flare 47 m up, 8-bit luma without/with): 25 m out 16.5/31, 50 m 16/21, 100 m 14/14, 200 m 12/12, sky 23/23 (no exposure change).
source_ref: Branch dines/illumination-flares (after review of af06dd92). Encoded VP9 CRF 38 with Playwright's ffmpeg (JPEG on pipe:0).
